newsitem.title: ITALY: U.S. to stage final Albania helicopter airlift.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to stage final Albania helicopter airlift.

text.p: The United States plans to stage its final evacuation mission later on Tuesday for foreign nationals stranded in troubled Albania, Commander Dave Anderson of the U.S. navy said.
U.S. marines had flown about 850 people out of Tirana since the operation started last Thursday, and the number of people still seeking assistance has declined to a trickle, he added.
"Our last helicopters flew in this morning and the final evacuation will fly out this afternoon."
It had not yet been decided whether to leave a contingent of marines at the U.S. diplomatic residential compound, where the airlift, codenamed Operation Silver Wake, was centred, he said.

U.S. Sea Stallion and Chinook helicopters, escorted by Cobra combat helicopters, have flown numerous missions between Tirana and the south eastern Italian port of Brindisi, evacuating people from more than 30 countries.
Heavily armed marines, dug in around the large, exposed compound, provided cover for the operation.
